Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys Used 2024 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Coupe 3LZ ZER for $38,300 Under MSRP
27 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer/autoevolution
Man, do I like this E-Ray! It's not a top-spec car, but it's not lightly optioned either, and for $87,500 with 3,200 miles on the clock, this is a genuine steal. Maybe it could have done with some additional exterior carbon fiber aero bits, the highly expensive carbon fiber wheels or the Competition Sport bucket seats (if that's your preference), but at the end of the day, this is still a 3LZ ZER. As far as I'm concerned, it's got everything you need.
This settles it. I've come around to the E-Ray big time. They're starting to become cheaper, on average, than the Z06, and buyers are answering the call. We can talk about how superior the Grand Sport X is all day long (not to mention the ZR1X), but at the end of the day, most people just want to drive home after having struck a good deal - and they don't get much better than this.
So, this car retailed for $125,860 originally, and whoever bought it now (at auction) just paid nearly $40,000 under MSRP. Plus a buyer's fee, to be fair. Regardless, this might be the cheapest E-Ray we've ever seen and you're buying so much car for the money, it's crazy.
I know it doesn't have the enthusiast appeal of the Z06 with its high-revving flat plane crank V8, but the end-result is more or less the same when it comes to straight line performance. The Z06's 5.5-liter LT6 V8 is pushing down 670 hp while revving to 8,600 rpm, whereas the E-Ray boasts the same 6.2-liter LT2 V8 you'd find in the Stingray, albeit with a 160-horsepower electric motor at the front, for a total of 655 hp. It'll only rev to 6,600 rpm.
But it's got all-wheel drive, and you can drive it on electric power alone, and that's definitely worth certain considerations.
Aside from its Riptide Blue Metallic exterior, this E-Ray also comes with Carbon Flash accents, LED headlights, plus a set of Carbon Flash-finished 20" and 21" forged wheels rocking Michelin Pilot Sport 4S rubber and Edge Red-finished calipers over carbon-ceramic discs. There's also a front-axle lift system, while the seller added the Carbon Flash front splitter, a wicker bill rear spoiler extension, splash guards, and over-the-top-stripes.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Personally, I'd be perfectly comfortable removing the stripes, and maybe wrapping the car a different color - I'm not the biggest Riptide Blue Metallic fan. But to each their own.
Meanwhile, interior highlights include the heated and ventilated GT2 bucket seats in Jet Black Napa leather with Adrenaline Red contrast stitching, Torch Red seat belts, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a 10-speaker Bose sound system, head-up display, and a heated and leather-trimmed steering wheel.
As for performance, we already touched on that a little bit. I will add that in a straight line, the E-Ray can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 2.5 seconds (with a 1-foot rollout), before maxing out at 184 mph (296 kph).
